evidence: Both WhatsApp call sites, NotificationInterceptorService.kt lines 150 to 157 and WhatsAppResponder.kt lines 122 to 129, build AutoAcceptConfig with the same five keys in the same order, apply toInt to both ganancia keys, and pass km with the same 999.0 sentinel, so the prior third-copy finding is resolved and not re-emitted.

PicapAutoAcceptPolicy keeps byte-identical AUTO-ACCEPT strings, evaluates each type gate inside the lambda in the same sequence as HEAD with gate 3 only after the km switch is true, and leaves the global filter and trasladoOk block untouched; gradle reports compileDebugKotlin and BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Versus HEAD the only WhatsApp outcome differences are the intended unknown-km acceptance plus the accepted cond2 ceiling and threshold truncation edges, with no other divergence found in either WhatsApp path or in the evaluator short-circuit order.

findings.claim: Behavior-activated acceptance widening on both WhatsApp paths: with the km switch on and the threshold at or above 5.0, a message whose origen has no parseable km is now auto-accepted where HEAD rejected it. This is the user-approved Picap-parity change so it is capped at WARNING, but it enlarges the set of malformed or km-less messages that trigger auto-respond.
proof_refs: WhatsAppResponder.kt line 136 and NotificationInterceptorService.kt line 162 pass km with the 999.0 sentinel into evaluateAutoAccept, while HEAD guarded the third condition with a non-null kmRecogida check on both paths.
AutoAcceptEvaluator.kt line 66 returns accepted true for condition 3 when isKmEnabled is true and maxKm is at least 5.0, independently of the km argument it receives.
PicapParser.kt extractKmFromPickup already returns 999.0 when no km match is found, which is the semantic these two WhatsApp call sites now adopt.
